title: What the pieces are worth
line: Pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, and why the king has no number.

steps.text: Players count pieces in points: a pawn is worth 1, a knight 3, a bishop 3, a rook 5 and a queen 9.
The king has no number. It is never captured: the game ends before that, so the king is worth the whole game.
Tap every black piece worth 3 points.
steps.after: A knight and a bishop are worth about the same: 3 each.

steps.text: Your bishop can capture the rook or the knight, and no black piece could capture it back. Capture the piece worth more.

wrong.d3f5: The knight is worth 3. The rook is worth 5.

steps.after: You took 5 points and gave nothing.

steps.text: Both sides have the same pawns. Tap the piece that puts one side ahead.

wrong.c6: The knight is worth 3. The white rook is worth 5.

steps.after: The rook is worth 5, the knight 3: White is 2 points ahead.

summary: Pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. The king can never be captured, so it has no number.
